Trump surprised everyone with much softer stance against China. Today he announced that he considers a 10% tariff on Chinese imports, but only if Beijing does not agree a deal on TikTok. He also linked the tariff to fetanyl exports from China.

FT reports: [link](https://www.ft.com/content/ee0718ce-99c0-465c-9466-a435268aebf7)

* Trump ordered investigation into US-China trade rather than immediately imposing threatened 60% tariffs; suggested 10% tariff related to fentanyl starting February 1

* Markets reacted negatively: CSI 300 fell 1%, Hang Seng down 1.6%, offshore renminbi weakened 0.25%

* Xi and Trump held first phone call in 4 years, discussing trade, fentanyl, and TikTok; China sent Vice-President Han Zheng to inauguration

* Trump linked TikTok ownership to tariffs, suggesting 100% tariffs unless Beijing allows US entity to take 50% ownership

* Chinese officials appear more open to negotiations about TikTok's ownership, with foreign ministry indicating companies should decide independently

* Economists remain cautious about avoiding trade conflict, noting Trump's administration includes China hawks despite softer initial approach

* Beijing considering broader deal potentially covering trade, TikTok, and other issues, but prepared to retaliate if relations deteriorate
